intro.text: Dalinar Kholin's late wife, and the mother of Adolin and Renarin.
Dalinar Kholin's late wife and the mother of Adolin and Renarin, a woman from Rira who fled to Alethkar with her brother Toh.
Dalinar Kholin's late wife and the mother of Adolin and Renarin, a Riran woman who died when the Rift was burned.

items.text: Evi grew up in Rira with her brother Toh and owned a set of Shardplate she never used. At about nineteen she and Toh fled to Alethkar, offering the Plate for protection. Torol Sadeas suggested Dalinar marry her, and he agreed, Navani being beyond his reach. As her culture required a long courtship, they married only after three years, though she followed him on campaign throughout, pleading with him to be more peaceful.

Evi gave birth to Adolin in 1150, at home in Kholin lands, and raised him largely alone while Dalinar fought on the borders. After one of his visits she had a second son; when Dalinar didn't answer her letters asking for a name, she called him Renarin, meaning it as "Re, born unto Nar", though it came out as "one who is born unto himself".

When Adolin was five, Evi insisted on joining Dalinar on campaign, as other Alethi wives did, spending half of each year in the war camps and half in Kholinar with the sickly Renarin. By 1163 she and Dalinar were more at odds than ever; after a bitter fight, he promised they would return home after putting down the rebellion in Rathalas, and tried bargaining with its highprince, Tanalan.

Tanalan betrayed Dalinar and tried to kill him. When Dalinar returned, bent on revenge, he had Evi escorted somewhere safe, but she slipped into the city to plead with Tanalan for peace. Tanalan held her in his prison, and when Dalinar set the Rift ablaze, Evi died in the flames before he learned she was there.

Evi was given a proper burial. Dalinar claimed Tanalan's men had kidnapped her and that the Rift was burned in retribution; in time Sadeas took the blame for the burning. Haunted most of all by her voice, Dalinar sought out the Nightwatcher to ask forgiveness for his part in her death, and Cultivation took away all his memories of his wife.

For years Dalinar heard only rushing wind when anyone said Evi's name. Her memory returned after the True Desolation began; a voice that might have been hers told him she forgave him, and he confessed what he had done in his book. Adolin kept warm memories of her, carried her chain as a lucky charm and quietly nursed fury at his father on her behalf.

appearance.text: Evi is exceptionally tall, almost as tall as an Alethi, and willowy and somewhat frail. She has pale blonde hair and light golden skin, though neither is true Iriali gold, with matching light yellow eyes.

personality.text: Calm and averse to conflict, Evi is a dedicated pacifist who keeps urging her husband to reject the warlike ways of his kin, though she holds firmly to her convictions. A devout follower of the Iri religion, she takes on many Vorin customs, yet still treats the One as the highest deity.

Though she and Dalinar are poorly matched, Evi works hard to make their marriage succeed and never lets her children see her frustration with his darker side, telling them their father is an excellent man. She comes to truly care for him, aware that he doesn't return her feelings to the same degree.
